title: The Mini Moon
article:
Did you know that for the last two months, Earth has had a “mini moon”? 2024 PT5, was an asteroid that was temporarily orbiting Earth. It measured 11 meters, about the size of a school bus.. PT5 was composed mostly of basaltic materials suggesting a lunar origin. This asteroid wasn’t visible to the human eye and you needed a large telescope to observe it.

PT5 circled Earth for roughly 2 months from September 29th to November 25th. Scientists believe it will possibly fly by Earth again in January 2025 and 2055.

PT5 was briefly influenced by Earth's gravitational force, which temporarily altered its original path around the Sun. After completing one orbit, PT5 was released back on its original orbit around the Sun.

Events like these are important because they help us look at the structure, composition and orbit of asteroids. It also helps us understand how objects enter and leave Earth's gravitational sphere. This information can help us in the future for planetary defense against larger, more dangerous asteroids.
author: Ava Samuels
